name: What bathroom layout works best for a narrow addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the best floor plan for a long, narrow bathroom addition?
mainEntity.text: What is the best floor plan for a long, narrow bathroom addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrow bathroom additions work best when the fixtures are arranged to preserve a clear walking path. A single-wall layout is often the easiest solution because it keeps plumbing concentrated and reduces wasted circulation space. In very tight rooms, a shower is usually a better fit than a tub, and a wall-hung or compact vanity can help the room feel larger. Pocket doors or outswing doors are useful when standard door swings would collide with fixtures. The goal is to avoid a layout where the toilet, vanity, and shower compete for the same usable space. In Los Angeles homes where floor area is precious, a thoughtful narrow-bath design can make the addition feel much larger than its actual dimensions. Good lighting, a larger mirror, and light finishes can also reduce the boxed-in feel.
acceptedAnswer.description: For a narrow bathroom, a single-wall or galley-style layout often works best. Place the vanity near the entry, keep the toilet in a private but accessible zone, and use a shower rather than a tub if space is tight. Pocket doors and wall-hung fixtures can improve circulation.
